language_note: Turns are written in the plain Indian English NGO programme staff actually use on a call: 'what all', 'kindly', 'na', 'only' as emphasis, 'we are having'. No caricature, no transliteration.

turns.user: Hello, we are running a livelihoods programme in Valparai. What all data do you have for this place?
turns.note: Category 1: plain-language inventory plus a visual marker.

turns.user: What is this map actually showing? Kindly explain in simple words na, I have to tell my field team.
turns.note: Category 2: plain explanation of the visual, no jargon.

turns.user: This data is covering which years? And is it for the whole plateau or only some estates only?
turns.note: Coverage question; years should be stated concretely.

turns.user: Out of all this, which one is most useful if I want to understand worker income?
turns.note: Should route to the wage data in the user's own framing.

conversations.title: Vocabulary pickup: MGNREGA / mnrega / job work

turns.user: Kindly show me what public works data you are having for this area.
turns.note: Seeds the MGNREGA vocabulary that later turns re-spell.

turns.user: This mnrega thing, how many works are there in last few years?
turns.note: Category 3: misspelt term must connect, not bounce.

turns.user: In our office we just say job work only. So tell me na, this job work is increasing or decreasing?
turns.note: Category 3: everyday phrasing for the same thing; reuse the user's words.

turns.user: And which village is getting most of this job work?
turns.note: Drill-down inside the user's vocabulary.

turns.user: Same thing for women workers, any data on that?
turns.note: Either an honest gap for MGNREGA-by-gender or a real answer from estate labour.

conversations.title: Drill-down to rows with understandable framing

turns.user: Which villages have the most survey visits? Show rows please.
turns.note: Category 4: rows, plus prose that a programme officer can read.

turns.user: There is one column called effort. What it means actually?
turns.note: Category 4: esoteric header translated into prose.

turns.user: Kindly turn it around and show which village we visited least. We have to plan next round.
turns.note: Re-sort request in plain words.

turns.user: Give me one line I can put in our monthly report about this.
turns.note: Brevity under an explicit one-line request.

turns.user: Near Kadamparai there is one empty square on the map. Can you estimate how many jobs will be there?
turns.note: Category 5: interpretation in plain words, or exactly ONE clarifying question.

turns.user: Yes, the square just below Kadamparai village. Take it as 10.255, 76.965. Kindly estimate for that one.
turns.note: Category 5: an estimate with confidence stated in everyday terms.

turns.user: How much you are trusting this number? Be frank with me.
turns.note: Confidence restated without statistics jargon.

turns.user: If I put this in a proposal, what caveat I should write?
turns.note: Limitation carried into the user's own document.

conversations.title: Honest limits: school data is absent

turns.user: How many children go to school here? We need it for our education programme.
turns.note: Category 6: honest gap plus what data does exist.

turns.user: So you are saying there is no school data at all? Or maybe it is there but not matching?
turns.note: Category 6: non-match is not absence framing.

turns.user: Then what all is the closest to household level information you are having?
turns.note: Should land on the household survey effort data.

turns.user: Fine. Kindly note it down that we need school enrolment data for Valparai.
turns.note: Data request captured, not silently dropped.

conversations.title: General knowledge may frame, numbers must come from data

turns.user: Is 10000 rupees a month good income for a tea worker?
turns.note: Category 7: general context allowed, but it must be labelled as general.

turns.user: What the actual data is saying about tea worker wages here?
turns.note: Numbers now must be from the site's own records.

turns.user: So compared to what you said generally, this is high or low?
turns.note: The comparison must keep general context and data separate.

turns.user: Can you write two lines for our donor about this wage situation?
turns.note: Donor-facing prose stays honest and short.

conversations.title: Out-migration: orientation, drill-down and the user's own words

turns.user: What all is happening with people leaving this area for work? Any data on that?
turns.note: Everyday phrasing must reach the migration source.

turns.user: This migration, which occupation is leaving most?
turns.note: Drill-down by occupation.

turns.user: Show me the rows na.
turns.note: Terse request must still produce a table view.

turns.user: And the tea plucker people, same thing for them?
turns.note: Entity vocabulary reuse.

turns.user: Summarise in 3 simple points for our team meeting.
turns.note: Summary stays plain and short.
